channel.title: Kseniia's Good News
channel.description: Positive news from several sources, scored 0-10 for goodness and refreshed every six hours.

item.title: Nigeria reports no Ebola spread after imported case [6/10]
item.description: Nigeria has recorded no new Ebola cases since a woman arriving from Uganda tested positive last month, and her contacts finished 21 days of monitoring uninfected. (Goodness 6/10: Containment worked in Nigeria, while the wider outbreak continues.)

item.title: Infant in Dubai becomes seizure-free after experimental drug [6/10]
item.description: A baby in Dubai who had a seizure about every 13 minutes since birth stopped having seizures after receiving an experimental drug. Follow-up so far covers only weeks. (Goodness 6/10: Dramatic result for one child, but the treatment is experimental and the follow-up is short.)

item.title: Bengaluru startup converts office air conditioners into air purifiers [6/10]
item.description: Clairco, a Bengaluru startup, retrofits office air conditioners to purify air. The company says its technology benefits around 1.5 million people. (Goodness 6/10: Useful local innovation; the reach figure is the company's own claim.)

item.title: US voters approve $27 billion in transit measures [7/10]
item.description: Voters approved 22 of 27 transit ballot measures on November 3, worth about $27.4 billion for repairs and expansion of transit systems. (Goodness 7/10: Broad funding for public transport, though delivery depends on officials.)

item.title: Wastewater plant in New Jersey installs microplastics-capturing system [6/10]
item.description: A treatment plant in Atlantic City has installed a system designed by former Princeton students that traps microplastics before they reach the ocean, mimicking wetland plants. (Goodness 6/10: Promising pilot-style technology at a single plant so far.)

item.title: China starts world's largest liquid-air energy storage plant [7/10]
item.description: A demonstration plant in western China now stores renewable electricity by liquefying air, then releasing it to drive a turbine when power is needed. (Goodness 7/10: A large demonstration of cheap grid storage, though still a demonstration plant.)

item.title: Los Angeles bans new oil drilling and phases out existing wells [8/10]
item.description: The city council banned new oil drilling and will phase out existing operations within city limits over 20 years, after a decade of pressure from nearby residents. (Goodness 8/10: Meaningful health and climate gain for neighbourhoods near wells, with a long phase-out.)

item.title: Spain's Cantabrian brown bears have doubled in 20 years [8/10]
item.description: The Cantabrian brown bear population has roughly doubled over two decades to about 370 animals, and their range now covers around 6,500 square miles. (Goodness 8/10: Clear conservation recovery of a threatened species over two decades.)

item.title: Angolan villagers monitor hunting to protect Okavango source wetlands [7/10]
item.description: Villages in Angola's southeastern highlands appointed Watchers to enforce traditional hunting rules, protecting the wetlands that feed the Okavango system. (Goodness 7/10: Community-led conservation protecting an internationally important wetland.)

item.title: Women in Uttarakhand keep native bees in house-wall hives [6/10]
item.description: Households in India's Himalayan Uttarakhand region keep Indian honey bees in hives built into mud walls, mostly tended by women, helping sustain native bee populations. (Goodness 6/10: A traditional practice that supports native pollinators.)

item.title: Brazil publishes voluntary roadmap to phase out fossil fuels [6/10]
item.description: Brazil released a global roadmap for phasing out coal, oil and gas in three phases between 2028 and 2033. It is non-binding. (Goodness 6/10: Notable step, but voluntary and unenforced.)

item.title: Atacama Desert sees record flower bloom [6/10]
item.description: About 200 plant species have flowered in Chile's Atacama Desert, possibly its largest recorded floral display. (Goodness 6/10: Striking natural spectacle, but a rare weather-driven event.)

item.title: Assam venture makes paper from elephant and rhino dung [6/10]
item.description: Elrhino produces handmade paper and stationery from elephant and rhino dung, giving rural villagers an income. (Goodness 6/10: Creative livelihood tied to conservation, small scale.)

item.title: Villagers trained to handle tiger encounters in the Sundarbans [7/10]
item.description: Thirty-three local volunteers in Kultali, West Bengal, are being trained to respond safely when tigers enter villages. (Goodness 7/10: Protects both people and tigers, but limited to one area.)

item.title: Program breeds fireflies to restore Bali's populations [6/10]
item.description: The Bring Back the Light program breeds fireflies in captivity and releases them to rebuild wild populations in Bali. (Goodness 6/10: Active recovery effort for a declining insect.)

item.title: Over 27,000 orchids rescued from road project in Kerala [7/10]
item.description: Researchers moved more than 27,000 orchids from trees slated for felling and replanted them; about three-quarters survived two years later. (Goodness 7/10: Effective rescue with good survival rates.)

item.title: Electric hydrofoil ferries arrive in the US [7/10]
item.description: Hydrofoil ferries lift their hulls above water to cut drag, making battery power practical. San Francisco plans a fleet electrification worth about half a billion dollars. (Goodness 7/10: Practical clean-transport technology, still early in deployment.)

item.title: Reusable pads help Ethiopian girls stay in school [7/10]
item.description: Ethiopia imports all its sanitary pads, making them costly. Reusable pads help girls who cannot afford disposables keep attending school. (Goodness 7/10: Practical help for education access.)

item.title: Rural colleges add support for student parents [6/10]
item.description: Colleges are offering family study rooms, stipends and peer groups for student parents, though reliable data on their numbers is lacking. (Goodness 6/10: Helpful local support, scale still unclear.)

item.title: Teen builds free app to help read autistic communication cues [7/10]
item.description: A 15-year-old taught himself machine learning to create Kora, a free app helping caregivers interpret emotional cues. It has over 700 users in 12 countries. (Goodness 7/10: Helpful tool for families, though still small in reach.)

item.title: Scottish maerl seabeds recover after scallop dredging ban [8/10]
item.description: A decade after dredging was banned, maerl seabeds around the Summer Isles are thriving and supporting local fish stocks. (Goodness 8/10: Protection led to measurable recovery of habitat and fish.)

item.title: Glowworms return to North Yorkshire reserve [7/10]
item.description: A volunteer breeds glowworm larvae in his garden shed and releases them into a reserve where the insects had been absent for a century. (Goodness 7/10: Local species restoration, small in scale but successful.)

item.title: Kenyan women turn discarded synthetic hair into crafts [6/10]
item.description: Women in Kenya are reusing synthetic hair, which becomes waste after hairstyles are removed, to make handmade products. (Goodness 6/10: Small-scale waste reduction with income benefits.)

item.title: Trained dogs find invasive plants about 75% of the time [6/10]
item.description: German researchers trained volunteer handler-dog teams to locate invasive plants in the wild, with roughly three-quarters success. (Goodness 6/10: Promising low-cost tool for protecting native ecosystems.)
